# 1 Chronicles Chapter 5 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 372v–373r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/1CH_005_page_001.jpg, 1CH_005_page_002.jpg

---

**5:1** And-the-sons of-Re'uven, the-firstborn of-Yisra'el — for he [was] the-firstborn, but-when-he-defiled [bechallelo] the-bed [yetsu'ei] of-his-father, his-birthright [bekhorato] was-given to-the-sons of-Yosef son of-Yisra'el, and-not to-be-enrolled-by-genealogy [lehityaches] as-the-birthright. **5:2** For Yehudah was-mighty [gavar] among-his-brothers, and-as-prince [lenagid] from-him, but-the-birthright [ha-bekhorah] [belonged] to-Yosef.

**5:3** The-sons of-Re'uven, the-firstborn of-Yisra'el: Chanokh, and-Pallu, Chetsron, and-Karmi. **5:4** The-sons of-Yo'el: Shema'yah his-son, Gog his-son, Shim'i his-son, **5:5** Mikhah his-son, Re'ayah his-son, Ba'al his-son, **5:6** Be'erah his-son, whom Tilgat-Pilne'eser king of-Ashur carried-away-into-exile [heglah]; he [was] a-prince [nasi] of-the-Re'uveni.

**5:7** And-his-brothers by-their-families, in-the-enrollment-by-genealogy [behityachsam] according-to-their-generations [letoldotam]: the-head [was] Ye'i'el, and-Zekharyah, **5:8** and-Bela son of-Azaz son of-Shema son of-Yo'el — he dwelt in-Aro'er and-unto Nevo and-Ba'al-Me'on. **5:9** And-to-the-east he-dwelt unto the-entering of-the-wilderness from the-river Perat [Euphrates], for their-livestock had-multiplied [ravu] in-the-land of-Gil'ad.

**5:10** And-in-the-days of-Sha'ul they-made war with-the-Hagri'im, and-they-fell by-their-hand, and-they-dwelt in-their-tents upon all the-face of-the-east of-Gil'ad.

**5:11** And-the-sons of-Gad dwelt opposite-them in-the-land of-ha-Bashan unto Salkhah. **5:12** Yo'el [was] the-head, and-Shafam the-second, and-Ya'nai, and-Shafat in-ha-Bashan. **5:13** And-their-brothers according-to-the-house of-their-fathers: Mikha'el, and-Meshullam, and-Sheva, and-Yorai, and-Ya'kan, and-Zi'a, and-Ever — seven. **5:14** These [were] the-sons of-Avichayil son of-Churi son of-Yaro'ach son of-Gil'ad son of-Mikha'el son of-Yeshishai son of-Yachdo son of-Buz. **5:15** Achi son of-Avdi'el son of-Guni [was] the-head of-the-house of-their-fathers. **5:16** And-they-dwelt in-Gil'ad, in-ha-Bashan and-in-its-daughters [benoteyha], and-in-all the-pasture-lands [migrashei] of-Sharon upon their-going-forth [totse'otam].

**5:17** All-of-them were-enrolled-by-genealogy in-the-days of-Yotam king of-Yehudah, and-in-the-days of-Yarov'am king of-Yisra'el.

**5:18** The-sons of-Re'uven and-the-Gadi and-the-half of-the-tribe of-Menasheh, from the-sons of-valor [benei chayil], men bearing [nose'ei] shield and-sword and-bending [dorkhei] bow and-trained [lemudei] of-war — forty-four thousand seven hundred and-sixty, going-out [yotse'ei] to-the-host [tsava]. **5:19** And-they-made war with-the-Hagri'im, and-Yetur, and-Nafish, and-Nodav. **5:20** And-they-were-helped [vayye'azru] against-them, and-were-given [vayyinnatnu] into-their-hand the-Hagri'im and-all who [were] with-them, for to-God [le-Elohim] they-cried-out [za'aqu] in-the-battle, and-he-was-entreated [ne'etar] by-them, for they-trusted [batchu] in-him.

**5:21** And-they-took-captive [vayyishbu] their-livestock: their-camels fifty thousand, and-sheep two hundred and-fifty thousand, and-donkeys two thousand, and-lives-of-men [nefesh adam] one hundred thousand. **5:22** For many [rabbim] fallen [chalalim] fell, for from-God [me-ha-Elohim] [was] the-war [ha-milchamah]. And-they-dwelt in-their-place until the-exile [ha-golah].

**5:23** And-the-sons of-the-half of-the-tribe of-Menasheh dwelt in-the-land, from-ha-Bashan unto Ba'al-Chermon and-Senir and-Mount Chermon. They multiplied [ravu].

**5:24** And-these [were] the-heads of-the-house of-their-fathers: and-Efer, and-Yish'i, and-Eli'el, and-Azri'el, and-Yirmeyah, and-Hodavyah, and-Yachdi'el — men mighty of-valor [gibborei chayil], men of-name [anshei shem], heads of-the-house of-their-fathers.

**5:25** And-they-acted-treacherously [vayyim'alu] against-the-God of-their-fathers, and-they-prostituted-themselves [vayyiznu] after the-gods of-the-peoples of-the-land whom God had-destroyed [hishmid] before-them. **5:26** And-aroused [vayyya'ar] the-God of-Yisra'el the-spirit [ruach] of-Pul king of-Ashur and-the-spirit of-Tilgat-Pilne'eser king of-Ashur, and-he-exiled-them [vayyaglem] — the-Re'uveni and-the-Gadi and-the-half of-the-tribe of-Menasheh — and-he-brought-them to-Chalach and-Chavor and-Hara and-the-river of-Gozan, unto this day.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.1-2 — Reuben's lost birthright:** The Chronicler explains a theological puzzle: the firstborn lost his rights (*bekhorah*) because he defiled his father's bed (Genesis 35:22). The birthright went to Joseph (the double portion — Ephraim and Manasseh), but the princely leadership (*nagid*) went to Judah. This separation of birthright and rulership is unique to Chronicles.

**v.6 — Tiglath-pileser:** Called *Tilgat-Pilne'eser* here — a variant spelling of the Assyrian king Tiglath-pileser III (r. 745-727 BCE), who deported the trans-Jordanian tribes circa 732 BCE.

**v.20 — "he was entreated by them":** The niphal of *atar* — a key Chronicler verb. God responds to prayer in battle. The pattern is: cry out → trust → divine response. This is the Chronicler's theology of war distilled to a single verse.

**v.25-26 — Ma'al (treachery):** The verb *ma'al* is the Chronicler's key word for covenant unfaithfulness. It triggers exile — the ultimate consequence. The "spirit" (*ruach*) of Assyria's kings is stirred by Israel's God; even pagan empires serve YHWH's purposes.

*— EMET*
